first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, and prior evidence suggests that reducing onboarding and signup friction improves time-to-value and first-week activation. Verify the two most directly relevant records before testing. Run a guarded simplification experiment with downstream monitoring of qualified activation, retention, and account quality so a volume lift does not mask lower long-term revenue value.

final.rationale: Run a small, guarded onboarding simplification test focused on SMB self-serve accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses both current problems: shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and retention, while signup simplification improved SMB activation and qualified revenue. Because signup simplification slightly reduced 30-day retention and has not been validated beyond SMB, monitor qualified revenue, activation quality, retention, and segment mix—not completion alone—before scaling.
